title: Same-Name Replacement ConfigMap (fast-recreating analog of F1.1/F1.2)

p_binding.description: Reusable name still resolves to the decision-time UID.

p_target_resolves.description: Queued name resolves to a concrete resource at actuation.

transitions.title: Attacker deletes and recreates f1-target under the same name
transitions.notes: Real transition duration is measured live, not simulated; recorded per trial.

provenance.platform_basis: Kubernetes ConfigMaps have immutable UIDs; a replacement object created under the same name receives a new UID, exactly the same identity-rebinding mechanism as F1.1/F1.2's Pod, but without container scheduling/image-pull/start latency.
provenance.incident_basis: Autonomous response queues quarantine after confirmed compromise, identical to F1.1/F1.2.
provenance.policy_basis: Historical compromise still applies to the original object; response must remain bound to the original UID.
provenance.limitations: This scenario exists specifically to test whether the F1 same-name-rebinding mechanism can be exercised within a live deadline; a ConfigMap is not a workload, so this does not itself demonstrate quarantining a real running process -- it isolates the identity-rebinding mechanism's timing from container-runtime overhead, which was the actual cause of F1.1/F1.2's 39-80s live transition times against a 5s deadline in the original E13 run.

notes: E23 F1-fast-rebinding extension: deadline-feasible live replication of the F1.1/F1.2 mechanism, motivated by the reviewer finding that F1.1/F1.2's real transition duration (39-80s) made them structurally unable to complete within their 5s frozen deadline.
